title: Dummies Will Resign: The Final Knight Fork
summary: Recognize the final checking fork once the bishop sacrifice has drawn the queen to f4.

nodes.question: Can White win the queen before the a-pawn needs to move?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Qxf4 has captured White’s bishop. White has Kb3/Nc3/a5 against Kc1/Qf4/f6/h7. The queen and king share the knight’s fork geometry.

branches.title: Fork first, then take the queen
commentary: Begin after ...Qxf4 has captured White’s bishop. White has Kb3/Nc3/a5 against Kc1/Qf4/f6/h7. The queen and king share the knight’s fork geometry.
Ne2+ checks Kc1 and attacks Qf4. The check gives Black no time to move the queen.
Kd2 answers the knight check. This is the illustrated king escape.
Nxf4 captures the queen. The exact knight-and-pawn versus two-pawn ending is winning for White; promotion and full conversion are outside this short pattern lesson.
branches.explanation: Nxf4 captures the queen. The exact knight-and-pawn versus two-pawn ending is winning for White; promotion and full conversion are outside this short pattern lesson.

branches.title: Independent pawn push misses the fork
commentary: Begin after ...Qxf4 has captured White’s bishop. White has Kb3/Nc3/a5 against Kc1/Qf4/f6/h7. The queen and king share the knight’s fork geometry.
a6 spends the forcing tempo on the pawn. The exact resulting position is winning for Black; White needed the checking fork before the queen could escape.

branches.title: Independent knight retreat misses the fork
commentary: Begin after ...Qxf4 has captured White’s bishop. White has Kb3/Nc3/a5 against Kc1/Qf4/f6/h7. The queen and king share the knight’s fork geometry.
Nb1 moves the knight away from the checking-fork square and gives up the exact win. Black is now winning with best play; the exposed king and queen no longer form an immediate Ne2 fork.

exercises.prompt: Why must the knight check while attacking the queen?
exercises.answer: A queen attack alone would let the queen escape. Ne2 checks the king and attacks f4 at the same time, forcing a king reply before White captures the queen.

startContext: This short final-pattern lesson begins in the supported seven-piece diagram after ...Qxf4 at 75s. It checks Ne2+/Kd2/Nxf4 and two independent wrong moves. The earlier larger queen/rook trades, Bg3 and Bf4 bishop offer remain source context; these final checks do not certify that complete setup. The source continues to the winning six-piece knight ending, whose exact outcome is checked without assuming a particular later pawn race.
